body.cap: A scene from CES 2025 Pangyo Lunch Talk | Photo by AVING NEWS

body.x: Gyeonggido Business and Science Accelerator (GBSA) introduced various startup support programs at the 'CES 2025 Pangyo Lunch Talk' held on the 20th, aiming to assist companies in expanding into the global market.

The event was designed to share innovative technologies from Pangyo-based companies participating in CES and create opportunities to expand business prospects in the global market. GBSA and AVING NEWS hosted it jointly on the second floor of the Gyeonggi Startup Campus at 'THE LINK' from 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM. Around 50 representatives from CES participant companies and Pangyo-based enterprises attended, with various firms presenting their CES experiences and technologies.

Presenting companies included UNIUNI, Aram HUVIS, and MEDIAIPLUS. UNIUNI was recognized with a CES Innovation Award for its deep-learning solution, 'SAVVY Accessible Restroom,' designed to enhance restroom safety and privacy for people with disabilities. Aram HUVIS introduced an AI-based personalized scalp care solution, leading innovations in the smart healthcare sector. MEDIAIPLUS showcased its clinical trial chatbot, which aims to expand global clinical trial accessibility.
Daesik Choi, Head of GBSA’s Techno Valley Planning Team, stated, "We have numerous support programs, and today, we wanted to introduce some of the smaller initiatives as well."

Choi, who took office at GBSA on January 1, emphasized GBSA’s proactive efforts in supporting startup companies’ global expansion. He highlighted booth support programs for startups participating in international exhibitions like CES and mentioned other startup support initiatives.

body.cap: Daesik Choi, Head of Gyeonggido Business and Science Accelerator Techo Valley Planning Team | Photo by AVING NEWS

body.x: One key program Choi emphasized was the Global Startup Commercialization Support Program, which offers up to 50 million KRW in funding to startups established within seven years in Gyeonggi Province. The support covers personnel expenses, product development, prototype production, intellectual property acquisition, promotional video production, and market expansion. Funding is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Choi urged attendees to share information about these programs with other startups, stating, "Many companies are still unaware of these opportunities." He added, "GBSA is committed to helping startups enter the global market through various initiatives."

GBSA continues to run numerous startup support programs this year. Choi noted, "GBSA alone operates hundreds of projects, including market expansion, international business development, and exhibition participation support." He also emphasized the agency’s role in facilitating overseas expansion through trade show participation and global marketing programs.

body.cap: Headquarters of Gyeonggido Business and Science Accelerator at Pangyo | Photo provided by GBSA

body.x: Additionally, GBSA offers cutting-edge technology spaces within Pangyo Techno Valley, including AI and 3D printing facilities, and provides extensive support for startups utilizing these resources. Choi explained, "These support initiatives help startups supplement their financial constraints and leverage essential technologies."

Funding remains one of the biggest challenges for startups. GBSA’s financial support programs aim to ease this burden by providing indirect financial assistance and offering opportunities to resolve funding issues through various enterprise support initiatives.
Choi encouraged companies to visit the GBSA website to explore the wide range of ongoing programs and noted, "There are hundreds of initiatives available to assist businesses."

He concluded by expressing his gratitude to the attendees, hoping the event would benefit their businesses. The event allowed companies to learn about GBSA’s diverse support programs and gain valuable insights into startup growth and global expansion.
Meanwhile, Pangyo Techno Valley will launch an overseas promotional project in 2025 to solidify its position as a global technology hub.

As part of this initiative, 'Global Media Meetups' will be held four times yearly to strengthen partnerships with international media. These meetups will provide direct networking opportunities between journalists, media representatives from key countries, and Pangyo-based companies, conducted through on-site interviews and virtual meetings via ZOOM. The project aims to attract international media attention and showcase Pangyo Techno Valley’s technological innovations and business growth.
A dedicated team will be assigned to manage content production and media outreach, ensuring the continuity of Pangyo Techno Valley’s global promotional efforts.

Through this global promotional initiative, Pangyo Techno Valley aims to establish itself as a key hub for technological innovation and expand opportunities for domestic companies to enter the international market. The project is expected to enhance its brand value abroad and attract global investment through strategic promotional activities.
GBSA affirmed its commitment to supporting startups through various initiatives, ensuring that companies within Pangyo Techno Valley can successfully expand globally.
